questions.question: Name the three conditions necessary for a mid-latitude cyclone to form, and state the direction of circulation around the low in the Southern Hemisphere.
questions.expected_answer: A polar front with a sharp temperature contrast between cold polar air and warm subtropical air; rotation supplied by the Coriolis force, which deflects moving air to the left in the Southern Hemisphere; and upper-air divergence by the jet stream, which removes air from the top of the system and lowers surface pressure. Air circulates clockwise around the low in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.question: Describe the three stages of development of a mid-latitude cyclone and explain why the system dies after occlusion.
questions.expected_answer: Initial or wave stage: friction between the opposing air flows kinks the polar front into a shallow wave. Mature stage: the wave deepens into an open system with a distinct warm front, cold front and warm sector between them. Occlusion stage: the faster cold front catches the warm front and lifts the warm sector off the surface. With its supply of warm surface air cut off, the temperature contrast disappears and the system weakens and dissipates.

questions.question: Describe the weather sequence experienced in Cape Town before, during and after the passage of a cold front, including the wind changes.
questions.expected_answer: Before: mild to warm humid conditions in the warm sector, north-westerly wind, steadily falling pressure, cloud building in the west. During: heavy showers from cumulonimbus, possible thunder, snow on the mountains, and the wind swings from north-west through west to south-west. After: temperature drops sharply, pressure rises as the South Atlantic High ridges in, cold gusty south-westerly winds, and clearing cold showery weather.
